issues.legal_issue: A compromise made during execution proceedings that postpones execution in return for payment of interest above the rate in the decree may be enforced in execution when it is properly recorded.
material_facts: A decree required payment of a sum with interest at a specified rate, and the judgment-debtor failed to pay as required.
During execution proceedings, the parties agreed to postpone execution for two months in return for payment of the outstanding amount with higher interest until payment.
The executing court recorded the compromise within the prescribed period, and the court regarded it as a fair bargain involving reasonable interest.
issues.conclusion: The agreement to pay higher interest was enforceable in execution proceedings.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 47 and Order 21, rule 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the executing court has exclusive power to determine questions relating to execution and may record and enforce a compromise adjusting rights and obligations under a decree, provided the adjustment is recorded. Order 23, rule 4 does not displace that power, and Order 20, rules 3 and 11 do not prevent enforcement of a reasonable term postponing payment. The Court relied on The Oudh Commercial Bank Ltd. v. Thakurain Bind Basni Kuer, Sreeshteedhur Shaha v. Woomeshnath Roy, Lakshmana v. Sukiya Bai, and Pradyumna Kumar Mullick v. Dinendra Mullick; it overruled Mr. Hasan Khan v. Motilal.

rule.if: execution_proceeding and compromise_relates_to_execution and compromise_recorded_in_time and (postponement_for_higher_interest or other_execution_adjustment) and reasonable_bargain

predicates.execution_proceeding: The dispute arises in proceedings to execute a decree.
predicates.compromise_relates_to_execution: The parties made an agreement concerning their rights or obligations in carrying out the decree.
predicates.compromise_recorded_in_time: The court recorded the compromise within the applicable period for recording it.
predicates.postponement_for_higher_interest: The agreement postponed execution in return for interest above the rate specified in the decree.
predicates.other_execution_adjustment: The agreement otherwise adjusted the parties' rights or obligations concerning execution of the decree.
predicates.reasonable_bargain: The court found the compromise to be a fair bargain with reasonable interest.

issues.definition: When an execution proceeding concerns a timely recorded, reasonable agreement about carrying out the decree, the agreement is enforceable in execution, including when it postpones execution in return for higher interest.

issues.legal_issue: A court that passed a decree may order postponement of its execution on agreed terms, and an order granting that postponement remains enforceable unless set aside.
material_facts: The court that passed the decree was also the court in which execution proceedings were brought.
The parties' petition sought a two-month postponement of execution rather than payment of the decretal amount by instalments.
The court recorded the agreed postponement and its interest term; the order had not been set aside.
issues.conclusion: The compromise was also enforceable because the court could order postponement on the agreed interest term, and its order was binding unless set aside; the instalment-application limitation period did not apply to a petition seeking postponement rather than instalments.
issues.legal_principle: Order 20, rule 11 permits the court passing a decree to postpone payment on terms as to interest. The Court held that the limitation period in Article 175 of the Indian Limitation Act, 1908, for an application seeking payment by instalments did not apply to a petition seeking postponement of execution. It further held that an order on the petition remained binding until set aside and could be enforced in execution, relying on Monmohan v. Khalishkhali Cooperative Bank.

rule.if: execution_proceeding and decree_court_is_execution_court and petition_seeks_postponement_not_installments and postponement_order_made and (instalment_limit_not_applicable or postponement_order_unset_aside)

predicates.execution_proceeding: The dispute arises in proceedings to execute a decree.
predicates.decree_court_is_execution_court: The court hearing execution is the court that passed the decree.
predicates.petition_seeks_postponement_not_installm: The application seeks to defer execution rather than to pay the decretal amount by instalments.
predicates.postponement_order_made: The court ordered postponement on the agreed terms, including the interest term.
predicates.instalment_limit_not_applicable: The time limit for applying to pay by instalments does not govern the application because it seeks postponement instead.
predicates.postponement_order_unset_aside: The postponement order has not been set aside.

issues.definition: When the decree court orders postponement in an execution proceeding on an application seeking postponement rather than instalments, the order is enforceable if the instalment-application time limit does not apply or the order remains unset aside.
